study: qal/mblocks -- two REAL packet/DSP blocks (CRC-32 of a 32-bit word; 8x8 unsigned array multiplier with Dadda CSA tree + Kogge-Stone final adder; 16x16 attempted after) mapped onto the committed three-phase trapezoid wave (qal/mesh3 5b9d05b: T_third=92 ps, d=3 nand-levels per bank, 1.65 V, bank k on phase (k-1) mod 3, outputs direct-wired, no registers). Measured against the same nand2/inv netlist pipelined in CMOS. Speed is the question (user direction); energy is REPORTED, never gated.
written_before_any_deck: This file is the first file in qal/mblocks/. Every cell choice, harness definition, window, threshold and predicted number below is fixed BEFORE mblocks.py exists and BEFORE the first simulation.

engines.primary: VACASK 0.3.4 (/usr/local/bin/vacask), PSP103 via /usr/local/lib/vacask/mod/psp103v4.osdi, cards qal/p620a/vacask_port/sg13g2_models.inc (kestrel tt, verbatim minus the 10 Xyce-ignored params). Port rules honoured (OFFSET_TABLE/SKEPTIC_AMENDMENTS): never icmode=uic (icmode=op, no forced ic needed -- no pre-charged islands in these decks); gear + reltol=1e-5, default abstol/chgtol (Xyce-tight tolerances collapse the stepper); step 0.1p maxstep 0.25p (committed accuracy convention); energies/charges ONLY by offline trapezoid on the engine's own grid (offline_meter convention), identically on both engines; NO FIND-AT cross-engine comparisons -- all instants are read offline from waveforms on a 0.10 ps grid (mesh3 extractor convention).
engines.cross_check: Xyce DEVELOPMENT-202609292309 (PyMS PSP103, own PYMS_VAE_CACHE under the scratchpad) on ONE anchor row per block: the SAME deck emitted in Xyce syntax, run to a truncated stop (first 6 periods) and compared wave-for-wave on the waves both engines ran (2..5): value bits, commit instants, eye widths, margins at commit, per-third rail charge. Pre-stated cross-engine bands (carried from OFFSET_TABLE): instants 1 ps, margins 1%, charges 2%.
engines.harness_anchor_IC: Before any block deck is trusted: the committed mesh3 trap_tt92_d3 (inverter banks, NB=6, P0-alt) is regenerated by THIS generator in VACASK syntax and scored by THIS extractor. PASS = value 144/144, worst margin_at_commit within 1% of 509.67 mV, worst overlap within 1 ps of 37.021 ps, standing eye within 1 ps of 129.03 ps, bank-1 Q_rise within 2% of 155.585 fC. Anything else stops the campaign (harness bug or engine fork).

ASSUMED.mesh_in_place: Carried standing licence (qal/mesh, qal/mesh3): each phase is a DRIVEN ideal trapezoid behind 0.001 ohm (ideal mesh = a BOUND). Per-bank per-third charge/energy books REPORTED as the mesh interface spec. The flat-top driver's measured 2.2x energy price (qal/meshdrv) applies and is not re-measured here.
ASSUMED.ideal_head: Bank-1 inputs (data+state words) are ideal full-swing PWL sources with 2 ps edges, BOTH polarities available at the head for free (dual-rail XOR needs a~ and b~). IDEAL-SOURCE BOOKING, stated: the head's fanout (up to 20 trees x 2 polarities per CRC input bit) and the head inverters are NOT charged to the wave. The CMOS comparator is given the same free head (its inputs are register outputs anyway).
ASSUMED.receiver_of_last_bank: mesh3 convention: the last bank's link is scored against the DERIVED ideal next-phase rail trip (same phase as the would-be next bank), labeled DERIVED; interior links are REAL (the next bank's measured rail).
ASSUMED.crc_recurrence: The CRC state feedback is NOT closed in the wave: a block update (next_state = F(state, data)) has latency >> one period (3*T_third), so one lane sustains one result per period only when ceil(latency/period) INDEPENDENT streams (packets/flows) are interleaved -- the standard packet-processing arrangement. The per-lane throughput number is therefore a streaming/interleaved figure, stated as such. Same statement for a FIR MAC accumulator loop (the multiplier is the inner-loop body; the accumulate is a separate adder stage, not built here).
ASSUMED.electrical_decomposition_CRC: The 32 CRC output trees share NO internal node (no subexpression sharing is used); their only shared nodes are the ideal head sources and the ideal phase rails (0.001 ohm series). The full circuit is therefore the electrical UNION of the trees and may be simulated in groups of trees in separate transients; group results (value, margins, eyes, commit instants) are exact per tree and per-bank charges SUM across groups. Residual coupling through the 0.001 ohm series resistance is bounded: |I_rail| x 0.001 ohm < 1e-5 V at mA-class currents. This is an ELECTRICAL identity, not an approximation, GIVEN the ideal mesh and ideal head already assumed; it is stated so the reader can reject it together with those assumptions. The multiplier cannot be decomposed (shared partial products) and is run monolithically.

cells_and_netlist.nand2: sg13g2_nand2_1 vendor transistor sizing VERBATIM = campaign inverter widths: pMOS 2 x w=1.12u l=0.13u in parallel (source+bulk on the bank's phase node), nMOS 2 x w=0.74u l=0.13u in SERIES (bottom source+bulk on the bank's metered ground). Stack depth 2 (nMOS) / 1 (pMOS): SHALLOW per the committed rule (nand2/and2 fine; nor2 and o21ai excluded). CL = 2 fF per gate output to the bank's ground (committed). Every real fanout (gate inputs of the consumers) loads the node in addition to CL.
cells_and_netlist.inverter: campaign-standard restoring inverter VERBATIM (wp 1.12u / wn 0.74u / l 0.13u, CL 2 fF) -- used ONLY as a delay/polarity element where the bank-alignment rule needs it.
cells_and_netlist.xor2_choice: XOR2 = DUAL-RAIL nand2 form, depth 2: given a, a~, b, b~: y = nand(nand(a,b~), nand(a~,b)); y~ = nand(nand(a,b), nand(a~,b~)) -- 6 nand2, 2 levels, restoring, shallow. NOTE (correcting the tasking's arithmetic): the single-rail 4-nand2 XOR is depth THREE (n1=nand(a,b); n2=nand(a,n1), n3=nand(b,n1); y=nand(n2,n3)); the depth-2 nand2 XOR exists only with both input polarities, which the dual-rail tree supplies. The pass-gate XOR is BANNED (committed: no gain + crowbar). The vendor sg13g2_xor2_1 contains a 2-high pMOS stack (its internal NOR2) and is excluded by the shallow-cell rule.
cells_and_netlist.full_adder: dual-rail nand2 FA, depth 4: x=a XOR b (dual, 6 nand2, levels 1-2); s = x XOR c (dual, 6 nand2, levels 3-4); cout = nand(nand(a,b), nand(c,x)) [nand(a,b) shared with the XOR], cout~ = nand(nand(a~,b~), nand(c~,x~)) [nand(a~,b~) shared] -- 16 nand2 per FA, both outputs and their complements at depth 4. Half adder: x dual (6) + c = inv(nand(a,b)) / c~ = nand(a,b) (nand shared) -- 7 gates. AND (partial product) = nand2 + inverter, dual: pp~ = nand(a,b), pp = inv(pp~) -- 2 gates, depth 2 (pp~ at depth 1).
cells_and_netlist.multiplier_B: 8x8 unsigned: 64 AND partial products -> Dadda reduction (heights 6,4,3,2) with the FA/HA above -> final adder Kogge-Stone (radix-2, nand2/inv only: g=and, p=xor dual at the PG level; prefix cells G = nand(g_hi~, nand(p_hi, g_lo)), P = nand(p_hi~,p_lo~)... each prefix level is 2 nand levels with polarity tracked; sum = p XOR carry_in dual). The 16x16 is attempted AFTER the 8x8 result is in, if the 8x8 wall time x4-6 fits; otherwise the 8x8 result is scaled by stated arithmetic (gate counts and levels are exact from the generator; the per-bank wave physics is per-bank, so banks count linearly).
cells_and_netlist.levelization_and_banking: ASAP nand-levels from the head (level 0 = head sources). bank(g) = ceil(level/3) (d=3 committed). Alignment rule (data in bank k is valid only to bank k+1): every edge u->g must satisfy bank(g) - bank(u) in {0, 1}; otherwise a delay chain of inverters is inserted from u, one per level, ending in bank(g)-1 (polarity: start from u~ when the chain length is odd and u~ exists; else one more inverter). Delay chains are shared per (source, level). ALL inserted inverters are real devices in the deck and in the gate/device counts. The bank count NB = ceil(max level / 3). Boundary set of bank k = every gate in bank k with a consumer in bank k+1 (for bank NB: the primary outputs); boundary sets are what the eye/margin/value scoring runs over (mesh3 scored the bank's last level; here boundary signals from interior levels are scored too, which is stricter).
cells_and_netlist.cmos_mapping: The SAME gate netlist (nand2/inv, delay inverters REMOVED since registers re-time) pipelined with a register every D nand-levels, D in {3, 6, 9, all}.

harness.timeline: T = 3*T_third. Word n (random 64-bit data+state for CRC; random (a,b) 8-bit pair for the multiplier; seed 20261016) is launched at the phase-A trough n*T with 2 ps edges, n = 0..NW-1, NW = 24. Bank k holds word n over [slot(k,n), slot(k,n)+2*T_third], slot(k,n) = n*T + (k-1)*T_third. Waves 0,1 are warm-up; waves 2..NW-1 (22 words) are scored -- every scored wave is a value check at every bank. tran end = (NW-1)*T + (NB-1)*T_third + 3*T_third + 50 ps.
harness.T_third: 92 ps (the certified mesh3 point). qal/mspeed/RESULTS.json does not exist at pre-registration time; if a faster CERTIFIED T_third appears there before the block runs finish, both blocks are re-run at it as a second row.
harness.scoring_carried_from_mesh3_VERBATIM_defi: Trip_S instantaneous-rail interpolation (qal/fcrit TRIP.json); margin sign by expected bit; eye = contiguous min-over-boundary-signals margin runs at 0 mV and 69.924 mV (3*sigma_total, MEASURED qal/eye/p2); 0.10 ps extraction grid with edge interpolation; commit_raw from the bank's OWN powered window [slot, slot+2*T_third]; die = close of the gated link eye run; overlap(link k) = t_die(k) - t_commit_raw(k+1); value = boundary word vs the receiver's instantaneous trip at the raw-validity midpoint; margin_at_commit both polarities; rising-side tracking lag reported. Model language: tracking lag / eye / margin at the sampling instant.
harness.latency_definition: end-to-end LATENCY(word n) = t_commit_raw(bank NB, wave n) - n*T  (first input edge at the head to the instant the final bank's complete output word is on the correct side of the receiver's instantaneous trip and stays there), reported with the gated (69.924 mV) commit alongside. The CMOS latency is stages x clock period (a result is available one clock after its last launch), stated with the comparator loads.
harness.throughput_definition: per-lane THROUGHPUT = one result per period 3*T_third = 1/(276 ps) = 3.623 Gresults/s at 92 ps, CONFIRMED by launching a new word every period and requiring all 22 scored words correct at the final bank. The wavefront level-rate (3 levels per 92 ps) is a DIFFERENT number (the bank initiation interval is 3*T_third, occupancy 1/3) and is never used as a throughput.
harness.charge_books: per bank, per third (rise/hold/fall), offline trapezoid of the phase source current on the engine's own grid, averaged over the scored waves; E likewise from v*i. Reported, not gated. Group runs (CRC) sum.

acceptance.A_value: every scored wave (2..NW-1), every bank: boundary word bit-correct at the raw-validity midpoint vs the receiver's instantaneous trip; at the final bank the word equals the SOFTWARE reference (Python CRC-32 IEEE 0x04C11DB7 MSB-first state update on the 32-bit word; Python a*b).
acceptance.B_eye: links 1..NB-1, every scored wave: min boundary-signal margin at the handoff commit sample >= 69.924 mV, both polarities.
acceptance.C_handoff: overlap(link k) > 0 for links 1..NB-1, every scored wave.
acceptance.PASS: A and B and C. The standing eye = mean 0 mV width of the last two REAL links if within 15% (mesh3 definition). Erosion sign reported per mesh3.
acceptance.cross_engine: Xyce anchor row agrees within the bands above on waves 2..5; disagreement outside band is REPORTED as an engine fork with the VACASK number carrying the engine label (never averaged).

cmos_comparator.form: period(D) = D * t_level + t_reg; results/s = 1/period; latency = ceil(L/D) * period, L = nand-levels of the block (delay inverters removed). t_reg(2 fF) = 315.378 ps DERIVED (linear between MEASURED 307.1 @ 0 fF and 335.7 @ 6.91 fF; liberty 1.11-1.21x optimistic => LOWER bound on the tax). Corner: + 100 ps clock uncertainty reported alongside.
cmos_comparator.t_level: MEASURED here, not assumed: a depth-12 nand2 chain at 2 fF per node (fcrit_skept sk_chain arm-D method: steady-state trip-to-trip per-level delay, 2 ps input edge), BOTH input-conditions (a=b switching together; one input tied high) at the campaign comparator supply 1.2 V (the 52.51 ps inverter reference point) AND at 1.65 V (iso-voltage with the wave rail -- the honest speed comparator; the 1.2 V number is the campaign's standing comparator). The worst of the two input-conditions is used. Run on VACASK and on Xyce (small deck, both engines, agreement reported).
cmos_comparator.sta: OpenSTA 3.1.0 + vendor liberty sg13g2_stdcell_typ_1p20V_25C.lib (the ALU anchors' flow) on the actual nand2/inv netlist written as structural Verilog (sg13g2_nand2_1 / sg13g2_inv_1), with sg13g2_dfrbp_1 registers inserted every D levels: report the minimum clock period per D directly from STA (clk->q + logic + setup, liberty pin loads, no wires). Reported next to the measured-t_level formula; the two are different comparators (liberty 1.2 V typ pin-loaded vs transistor-level 2 fF load-matched) and are labeled as such.
cmos_comparator.latency_claim_rule: Any latency statement names the comparator: (i) registered CMOS per D, (ii) the bare unregistered nand2 chain L * t_level at 1.2 V and at 1.65 V (the load-matched level comparator). The wave's per-level rate is NOT expected to beat the bare 1.65 V chain.

PREDICTIONS_before_first_deck.cell: nand2 CMOS chain level at 2 fF: 1.2 V: 60-75 ps (inverter 52.51 ps; 2-high nMOS stack + 2x input cap per fanout); 1.65 V: 38-48 ps. In-wave nand2 traversal (rising tracking lag of the last boundary level after the rail's 50%): 85-100 ps for 3 nand levels (inverter d=3: 77-81 ps measured), commit_raw at slot + 115..135 ps (inverter d=3: 110-117).

block_A_CRC32.structure: 32 trees, 24..34 terms each, 872 dual-rail XOR2 = 5232 nand2 (+ ~1-3% delay inverters), XOR depth 6 -> 12 nand levels -> NB = 4 banks, ~21k FETs total, run as 4 groups of 8 trees on VACASK (~5k FETs each).
block_A_CRC32.sustain: PASS A+B+C on all 22 scored words (the mesh3 d=3 point had 509 mV worst commit margin and 37 ps overlap with inverters; nand2 is slower, so worst margin is predicted 250-450 mV, overlap 15-35 ps, standing eye 105-125 ps). Failure mode if any: the deepest-fanout boundary nodes (a boundary nand2 driving 2-3 consumers) commit late -> overlap shrinks first on the link into bank 2.
block_A_CRC32.latency_QAL_ps: 3*92 + (115..135) = 391..411 ps end-to-end (first input edge -> final word committed).
block_A_CRC32.throughput_QAL: 3.623 Gresults/s per lane (one 32-bit word per 276 ps), all 22 scored words correct.

CMOS_D.3: period 495-540 ps (t_level 60-75 @1.2V) -> 1.85-2.02 G/s, latency 4 stages = 1.98-2.16 ns

block_A_CRC32.expected_ratios: throughput per lane QAL/CMOS: D=3 1.8-2.0x; D=6 2.4-2.8x; D=9 3.1-3.6x; D=all 3.7-4.4x (at 1.2 V comparator; at 1.65 V subtract ~15-25%). Latency: QAL 0.39-0.41 ns vs best registered CMOS (D=all) 1.04-1.22 ns -> QAL 2.5-3.1x shorter, BECAUSE the single flop tax (315 ps) is itself ~80% of the wave's whole latency; vs the BARE unregistered chain 12 x t_level = 0.72-0.90 ns @1.2 V / 0.46-0.58 ns @1.65 V the wave is at best at parity at iso-voltage (no per-level latency win claimed).

block_B_mul8x8.structure: 64 AND (128 gates), Dadda 8x8: 35 FA (560 nand2) + 7 HA (49), KS 14-bit (~200-260 gates), delay inverters (~150-300): ~1100-1300 gates, ~4.5-5.5k FETs; nand levels L = 2 (AND) + 4x4 (Dadda) + ~14 (KS: PG 2 + 4 prefix x 2 + sum 2) = 32-36 -> NB = 11-12 banks.
block_B_mul8x8.sustain: PASS A+B+C on 22 scored operand pairs; a 12-bank chain is the longest the wave has been asked to sustain (mesh3: 6) -- the erosion sign (SUSTAINS, asymptotic eye) is the pre-registered test of the standing-eye claim at 2x the proven chain length. Worst commit margin 200-400 mV (FA boundary nodes with fanout 3-4 are the worst nodes), overlap 10-30 ps.
block_B_mul8x8.throughput_QAL: 3.623 Gresults/s per lane (one 16-bit product per 276 ps).

CMOS_D.3: period 495-540 ps, 11-12 stages -> latency 5.4-6.5 ns, 1.85-2.02 G/s

block_B_mul8x8.expected_ratios: throughput per lane QAL/CMOS: D=3 1.8-2.0x, D=6 2.4-2.8x, D=9 3.1-3.6x, D=all 8-11x. Latency: QAL 1.0-1.25 ns vs registered CMOS best (D=all) 2.2-3.0 ns -> 2-2.5x shorter; vs the bare chain (32-36 levels x t_level) 1.9-2.7 ns @1.2 V / 1.2-1.7 ns @1.65 V -> parity to 1.4x at iso-voltage; the per-level wave rate does not beat the bare chain level at 1.65 V.
block_B_mul8x8.scaling_16x16: gate count ~4x (240 FA, 256 AND, KS 32-bit), levels +~6 (two more Dadda stages, one more prefix level) -> NB 13-14; throughput identical per lane; latency +2 banks (+184 ps). Run if ~20k FETs x ~28k points fits (c6288 anchor: 10k FETs at 70 ms/pt): predicted 1.5-3 h; attempted in the background after the 8x8 PASS.

PREDICTIONS_before_first_deck.where_the_win_lives: PREDICTED: the QAL win is in RESULTS/S PER LANE (one result per 3*T_third with NO register tax in the period) and in END-TO-END LATENCY VERSUS REGISTERED CMOS at any D (because t_reg 315 ps >= the wave's whole bank-to-bank step); it is NOT a per-level latency win against the bare load-matched CMOS chain at iso-voltage. Energy: per-bank rail books reported; the 2.2x flat-top price (meshdrv) stands.
PREDICTIONS_before_first_deck.engine_agreement: VACASK vs Xyce on the anchor rows: commit instants within 1 ps, margins within 1%, eye widths within 1 ps, charges within 2% (the tg15p offset table's classes); the committed harness-anchor (mesh3 trap_tt92_d3 re-extracted on VACASK) within the IC bands above.

wall_time_plan: <= 3 concurrent simulator processes. VACASK: mesh3 IC (288 FETs, 1.9 ns) ~1-2 min; CRC group (~5k FETs, 7 ns) ~15-25 min each x 4; mul8x8 (~5k FETs, 9.5 ns) ~25-40 min; Xyce anchors (truncated to 6 periods) ~30-60 min each in the background. Waveform archives live only in the scratchpad and are deleted after extraction; the repo keeps decks, OUT.json, RESULTS.json, README.md, PRE_REGISTERED.json.
